title: Selfish musicians in New York today
summary: Cobb complains that New York musicians keep to themselves, contrasting it with his own hospitality in Houston.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I've got some news for you. I just left New York. And I'm with a group of guys. We've got it going now all right. But it's the same difference. They go their own respective ways. They don't care nothing about you. But, see, if I didn't know my way around New York or Jersey, they would be treating me wrong, but I'm all right now. And today they're all selfish, and I can't understand selfish musicians.
When you come to Houston, I'm not selfish with you. I invite you to my house.
But you catch them and -- oh, when you come to New York, call them -- call them, they're busy doing nothing.
See what I say, I mean nothing.
